key_insight: The paper derives a principled occupancy field for 3D Gaussian Splatting and leverages oriented Gaussians to turn opacity-based 'blobs' into surface-aware 'spokes', enabling high-fidelity surface extraction from 3DGS representations.
problem_solved: 3D Gaussian Splatting excels at fast novel-view synthesis but lacks a global geometric field, making robust surface extraction difficult and forcing reliance on heuristic depth fusion; this work provides a theoretical and practical solution for extracting accurate surfaces from 3DGS.
method: Formulate a principled occupancy field for Gaussian Splatting inspired by the Objects-as-Volumes framework, transforming opacity blobs into a volumetric occupancy signal.
Introduce oriented Gaussians (spokes) to capture local surface orientation and geometry more faithfully than isotropic splats.

Use the derived occupancy field together with oriented Gaussians in a reconstruction pipeline to extract high-quality surfaces (e.g., mesh extraction from occupancy) compatible with existing 3DGS workflows.
impact: Bridges the gap between fast neural rendering and accurate geometry: practitioners can retain 3DGS's rendering speed while obtaining reliable surface reconstructions without ad-hoc heuristics, improving downstream tasks like 3D printing, AR/VR content, and geometry-based learning.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: original 3DGS blobs + heuristic TSDF mesh vs oriented Gaussians occupancy-derived mesh (before/after).
Diagram of an oriented Gaussian (spoke) showing center, covariance/orientation, and local surface normal alignment.
Pipeline flowchart: 3DGS model -> occupancy derivation -> oriented Gaussian fitting -> mesh extraction (marching cubes / iso-surface).
Error/quality heatmap or silhouette overlap comparing reconstructed mesh to ground-truth geometry.
paper_title: From Blobs to Spokes: High-Fidelity Surface Reconstruction via Oriented Gaussians
paper_authors: Diego Gomez, Antoine Guédon, Nissim Maruani, Bingchen Gong, Maks Ovsjanikov
